one_line_contribution: The claim is that the presence of an answer-bearing retrieved experience item in the demonstration slot causally suppresses per-episode compliance with an explicit, contemporaneous verification instruction — even on episodes where the agent does not copy the memory — and that instructions optimized with a bank in context therefore become bank-specific rather than generally better.
closest_prior_work: Xiong et al., arXiv:2505.16067 (experience-following), which the proposal concedes and tries to defeat with the non-echo subset test. The threat is larger than conceded. Experience-following is a graded similarity effect between retrieved output and emitted output, not a binary echo/non-echo switch. An agent can be pulled toward a stored answer, terminate its search early, and still emit a non-identical final answer — partial imitation, a stored answer that is wrong for this instance, or a paraphrase that the MEMORY-ECHO judge scores as non-matching. A surviving compliance deficit on the non-echo subset is therefore fully consistent with a graded output-imitation account, so Prediction 8 does not discriminate the two theories in the direction claimed; only a null there is informative, and the proposal has arranged its decisive test so that the outcome it predicts is the uninformative one. Worse, 'non-echo' is defined by an outcome that memory itself causes: the subset is selected post-treatment in the M1 arm and compared against unselected M0 episodes on the same instances. That is collider conditioning of exactly the kind the proposal itself disclaims in Risk 4 and Analysis 1, committed in the headline discriminating analysis. Separately, arXiv:2608.16032 ('Proof-of-Execution Memory') collides at symptom level and is handled well via the record-correctness audit, but I cannot verify that this ID exists (see preprint_collision).
strongest_objection: The centerpiece compliance measure is not separable from the mediator it is supposed to be independent of, so the 'veto' may be a relabeling of early termination rather than an instruction-slot phenomenon. I* requires the agent to cite spans retrieved in THIS episode that support the answer, and CITATION VALIDITY requires those spans to actually support it. Prediction 2 simultaneously asserts that evidence sufficiency drops >=12 points under M1. But an agent that truncated its search and never retrieved a supporting span CANNOT comply with a validity-checked citation requirement — non-compliance is entailed, not chosen. So the predicted >=25-point compliance collapse under M1 is partly a mechanical consequence of the >=12-point sufficiency drop that the same proposal predicts, and the paper's own arms cannot say how much of it is 'the agent stopped obeying the instruction' versus 'the agent had nothing left to cite.' Analysis 2 estimates unconditional compliance and never conditions on sufficiency, even though the instrumentation records both binaries per episode. The M0/M2 controls do not rescue this: those are precisely the conditions in which the agent searches longer and therefore has valid spans available, so the predicted 'high / high / collapsed' pattern is exactly what a pure truncation account with no instruction-slot mechanism would produce. As written, C2 is a restatement of Analysis 1's mediation result in a new vocabulary, and the paper's strongest rhetorical move ('the model can obviously execute the instruction, it does so under two conditions') begs the question, because under M0/M2 executing it is possible and under M1 it may not be.
what_would_fix_it: 1) Make the primary veto quantity CONDITIONAL: compliance with I* restricted to M1 episodes in which evidence sufficiency is 1 (supporting spans were in fact retrieved this episode), compared to the same conditional quantity under M0/M2. A deficit that survives conditioning on sufficiency is a genuine instruction-slot failure — the agent had the spans and declined to state them — and nothing else in the plan can produce that number. Report the unconditional gap as descriptive. 2) Add the slot-swap control described in missing_baseline so 'memory slot' is established as the operative object rather than 'a candidate answer anywhere in context.' 3) Add G1@M0. 4) Re-power or re-endpoint Stage 2: Prediction 13 asks the design to resolve a +3-point Delta and then to distinguish 40% retention of it (~1.2 points) from more, and to equivalence-test G0 across banks at a 2-point margin, while the Measurement section states the accuracy MDE at n=400 is ~5 points and that 'differences between 2 and 3 points are reported inconclusive.' By the proposal's own MDE table the practice-facing claim (4) is undecidable as designed. Either move Stage 2 to a high-signal per-episode binary endpoint (as was correctly done for the veto), raise n substantially for the bank-swap cells only, or state claim (4) as exploratory. 5) Reconsider the GEPA/MIPROv2 rollout budget: 350 rollouts against a 150-instance train split, in a track whose own documented re-scoring drift is 5-14 points, means the optimizer's retain-or-discard decision on the seeded I* is made on a selection signal at or below the study's measured noise floor. Prediction 10 and Analysis 5 then report a coin flip as a finding about the fitness landscape. Add the null-replicate treatment to the optimizer's own train-score trajectory, or budget the search so its selection is above noise.
missing_baseline: Two, both cheap. (a) G1@M0 — the instruction optimized WITH Bank A, evaluated with no memory. The plan runs G0@M0, G1@M1, G0@M1 and G1@Bank B but omits this cell, so the 2x2 that defines 'bank entanglement' is incomplete: without it you cannot distinguish an instruction that is specific to Bank A from one that is merely memory-conditional in general (i.e., degraded whenever any bank, or no bank, is present). A reviewer will ask for this in the first round and it costs one arm. (b) A SLOT-SWAP control: the identical answer-bearing text injected somewhere other than the memory/demonstration slot — appended to the query, or returned as one more retrieved document from the tool stack — at matched tokens. Every arm in the design varies content WITHIN the memory slot, so the plan can show that answer-bearing content truncates search but cannot show that its being memory is what matters. Without this control the result reduces to 'a plausible candidate answer in context short-circuits evidence gathering,' which is a known answer-leakage/shortcut effect and does not support the title's claim about the instruction slot's relationship to the memory slot. Note also that no arm establishes an upper bound on compliance (e.g., I* with a supporting span pre-inserted), so the 65% precheck floor is the only calibration for what 'high compliance' means.
preprint_collision: Procedurally this is one of the better collision checks I have read — it names four collisions, concedes the phenomenon outright, and ties each to a pre-registered numeric threshold that can go against the author (Predictions 3, 8, 13). That is genuine and I credit it. But it is not evidentially trustworthy, for a reason the proposal itself supplies: an earlier draft's novelty argument rested on arXiv:2605.24941 plus five sibling IDs, all of which turned out to be unverifiable and were flagged by three reviewers. The replacement set is structurally identical to the discredited set — 2601.09760, 2601.07470, 2603.21520, 2604.15774, 2604.27003, 2608.16032 — and every one is given as a bare arXiv number with a paraphrased finding and, unlike Xiong et al. (2505.16067, the sole entry with authors and a venue), no author list, no venue, no quoted result. A checker cannot confirm any of them from what is on the page. Given the demonstrated prior failure mode, the burden is on the author to present these with full bibliographic detail; as submitted, the entire positioning against 'Proof-of-Execution Memory,' MemEvoBench and MemAPO rests on citations with the same provenance as the ones already retracted, and claims (3) and (4) are differentiated exclusively against those three. Two further weaknesses: the 'Explicit gap, in the search's own terms' paragraph cites the search tool's summary of its own coverage as evidence that the gap exists, which is circular — a search summary reports what was retrieved, not what exists; and the caveats admit no ICLR/NeurIPS/ACL 2026-2027 submission-portal search was run, which for a fast-moving area at a September 2026 submission is where the scooping paper would most likely be. I do not know of a preprint that makes this exact conjunction of claims, but I cannot treat the novelty of claims (3) and (4) as established on this evidence.
